name: research-kit
description: Tools for research work, from reading papers to after publication: one skill each, so that an agent runs the tool and quotes what it found.

plugins.name: venue-atlas
plugins.description: What a conference was about, year by year: 60,000 papers of seven venues on maps by meaning, named topics with their trends, search by meaning in the browser.

plugins.name: paper-impact
plugins.description: Which papers at AI venues mattered: every NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR and ACL paper with its citations and field-normalized impact from OpenAlex, and how much OpenAlex covers.

plugins.name: table-trace
plugins.description: Every number in a paper's tables, read from its LaTeX source and traced to its cell; and what papers report for the same model on the same benchmark, side by side.

plugins.name: arxiv-diff
plugins.description: What changed between two versions of a paper: the result numbers in its tables by row and column, and the text, abstract, authors, figures and references.

plugins.name: gpu-budget
plugins.description: How much GPU memory, time and money training, fine-tuning or serving an LLM takes, each part with its formula (ZeRO/FSDP, parallelism, MoE, LoRA/QLoRA, KV cache), checked against published runs.

plugins.name: exp-tables
plugins.description: Experiment results to your paper's table: mean ± spread over seeds, significance against the best, bold only where the seeds support it; from CSV, wandb, TensorBoard or MLflow.

plugins.name: repro-score
plugins.description: Can someone reproduce your paper from your code? A score out of 100 for a research code repository, item by item with the file and line behind it, read from the files with nothing run.

plugins.name: fig-check
plugins.description: A paper's figures as they will print: text size at the printed scale, colours that collapse for colour-blind readers, raster resolution; for every figure of a LaTeX project.

plugins.name: paper-proof
plugins.description: Check your paper before reviewers do: invented or wrong references, bold results that are not the best, claimed gains that do not add up, stale abstract numbers, broken labels.

plugins.name: submit-check
plugins.description: Don't get desk-rejected for a slip: a LaTeX paper checked against the venue's rules (double-blind leaks, template mode, page limit, required sections, PDF fonts, leftover TODOs).

plugins.name: iclr-scores
plugins.description: What ICLR's review scores led to, 2017-2025: the acceptance rate by mean score, where half the papers got in, what disagreement did, and the odds for your scores.

plugins.name: paper-page
plugins.description: A project page for your paper from its arXiv id: links, teaser, abstract, BibTeX, Google Scholar and link-preview tags, in one static HTML file for GitHub Pages.

plugins.name: scholar-cards
plugins.description: Your citations, h-index and most cited papers from OpenAlex as SVG cards for an academic homepage or a GitHub profile, kept fresh by a GitHub Action; no API key.
